comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and JPM disclose increases in noninterest expense for 2024 driven by investments in people and technology. BAC’s noninterest expense rose $509 million due to 'continued investments in the business, including people, technology and operations.' JPM’s noninterest expense rose 9% to $38.0 billion, with drivers including 'higher compensation expense... increase in the number of employees, including in technology' and 'higher noncompensation expense, largely driven by continued investments in technology and marketing.' Both companies explicitly link expense growth to strategic investments in technology and human capital (employees/people), though JPM provides a more detailed breakdown of compensation vs. noncompensation and notes specific impacts like First Republic integration.

• higher noncompensation expense, largely driven by continued investments in technology and marketing, as well as higher operating losses, partially offset by lower legal expense.
